cards.title: Our Thing
cards.instruction: Protect one shared ritual, phrase, or tradition as the living proof that the relationship still exists.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two spoons for dessert. We still do our thing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we discuss the contract?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the first shared bite. Contracts shouldn't eat alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ordered my own pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then bring it here. Our thing can expand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we sign the shop over, two spoons. We always share dessert.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ordered my own. We're allowed separate puddings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. One shared bite first. We're selling the shop, not us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's coming in a takeaway box. My train leaves soon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll walk you to the station. Keep both spoons out.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 calls two spoons 'our thing'; A5 protects sharing, though the relationship's survival remains implicit.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 postpones B2's contract discussion; A5 incorporates B4's separate pudding.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants contract discussion and B4 wants separate dessert, but their relationship is unspecified.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands the dessert arrangement without increasing its emotional consequence.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies dessert spoons and B2 supplies pending business, making the encounter playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Contracts shouldn't eat alone' foregrounds a personification over A's sincere concern.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 explicitly makes the shared bite proof that selling the shop does not end their relationship.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's separate puddings become A3's shared first bite; B4's train changes A5's location for the ritual.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants separate dessert and B4 needs to travel; A3 and A5 accommodate both without surrendering connection.

heightening.evidence: A5 commits to walking to the station after B4 makes remaining at the table impossible.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a shop handover and two dessert spoons; B4 adds an immediately playable departure deadline.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Keep both spoons out' carries the emotional insistence through a concise physical detail.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 orders separately; A3 reduces the protected ritual to one shared bite.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 introduces takeaway packaging and an imminent train; A5 moves the shared ritual onto the station walk.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A3 states the relationship meaning of the spoons: 'selling the shop, not us.'
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A1 protects sharing at the table; A5 undertakes an additional journey to preserve it.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A protects a specific shared dessert ritual because performing it proves the relationship survives a business separation.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Sentimental nostalgia would value the dessert as a memory without needing to perform it now.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A1 says 'We still do our thing'; revised A3 explicitly separates selling the shop from losing the relationship.

records.recommendedEdit: The original's emotional stakes were thin. The revision introduces a shop sale and train departure. Separate internal coach-1.0 reread: fidelity 5 (A3 links sharing to continuity), logic 5 (A3 accepts B2's pudding; A5 follows B4's train), relationship 4 (B2 asserts independence), heightening 4 (A5 accompanies B), specificity 5 (A1 shop sale), brevityWit 4 (A5 preserves both spoons). Total 92; spoken ABABA and word-limit gates pass.

records.writerReservation: The shop sale makes the relationship stakes clearer, but the performers must supply whether this is friendship, romance or family.
records.alternativeComparison: Unlike the handshake alternative's refusal to yield to a taxi, this A accommodates departure and actively relocates the ritual.

cards.title: This Is How It Ends
cards.instruction: Treat every awkward pause, changed plan, or small disagreement as the possible beginning of permanent distance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You cancelled lunch. Should I leave my key?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have a dentist appointment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First lunch, then the key, then separate dentists.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep your key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For emergencies or belonging? I'm choosing which ring it goes on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep your key.

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: A Sign We’re Fine
cards.instruction: Interpret every laugh, favor, and familiar habit as evidence that the connection is stronger than appearances suggest.

cards.title: Composure on Loan
